ov: Soft, free-swimming sea animals with a bell-shaped body and stinging tentacles. They have no true brain and have existed for at least 500 million years, making them the oldest multi-organ animal group. They swim by pulsing the bell.

why.dg: Stings from some box jellyfish, such as Chironex fleckeri, are extremely painful and often fatal to people.
why.et: Some jellyfish are eaten, pressed and salted, as a delicacy in some Asian countries.

len: About 1 mm to nearly 2 m across the bell
rg: Seas worldwide; some similar-looking hydrozoans live in fresh water.
df: Prey caught with stinging tentacles; box jellyfish actively hunt small fish.
fx: Jellyfish sometimes gather in huge masses called blooms.
Box jellyfish have true eyes, with retinas, corneas and lenses.
notes: Group entry. ANSWER CHECK (fact): the animals.js fact "No brain, no heart, no blood, and older than the dinosaurs" is broadly right. Wikipedia says most jellyfish lack specialised circulation and a true brain, and they date back at least 500 million years.
